paper_title: ATPlace2.5D: Analytical Thermal-Aware Chiplet Placement Framework for Large-Scale 2.5D-IC

extraction.paper_title: ATPlace2.5D: Analytical Thermal-Aware Chiplet Placement Framework for Large-Scale 2.5D-IC

scenario.figure_or_table: Table 3 (Case 3 benchmark configuration); Table 6 (thermal-aware results); Fig. 5 (Case 3 layouts)
scenario.description: ATPlace2.5D benchmark Case 3. It has 8 dies (4 CPU and 4 DRAM chiplets), 8448 nets, a 39 mm x 39 mm interposer and 0.6 whitespace. Paper Table 6 reports Tmax of 92.3 C for ATPlace2.5D thermal-aware placement and 94.1 C for TAP-2.5D, taken as the maximum temperature over the HotSpot 6.0 steady-state thermal map. The pinned Case3 reference files supply chiplet dimensions and powers, but the .pl file holds only placeholder (0,0) coordinates, so no final placement is published in them.
scenario.architecture: 2.5D-IC: chiplets on a passive silicon interposer (TSVs, RDL, microbumps) on an organic substrate. Heat leaves through the primary path TIM, spreader and air-forced heatsink. Chiplets are 4 CPU and 4 DRAM with x32 UCIe advanced-package D2D links.
scenario.workload: Worst-case chiplet power distribution, steady state. Pinned Case3.power lists 150 W for each of the 4 CPUs and 20 W for each of the 4 DRAMs.
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state HotSpot 6.0 as golden simulator, 64x64 grid, ambient 45 C, heatsink convective resistance 0.1 K/W, adiabatic lateral surfaces, minimum chiplet spacing 100 um. Selected scenario: Case 3 thermal-aware optimization.

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 6.0 steady-state thermal simulation (64x64 grid) is the golden simulator (PDF p.3). A trained analytical Green's-function compact thermal model replaces it inside the optimization loop (PDF p.4-5).
original_setup.optimizer: ATPlace2.5D (PDF p.3-6). MILP (Gurobi) initialization, orientation-aware analytical placement by conjugate gradient descent with a thermal penalty R[T] and density penalty, MILP legalization, and Optuna Bayesian hyperparameter optimization.
original_setup.controller: None. This is a design-time steady-state placement flow with no runtime or dynamic thermal controller.
original_setup.benchmark: ATPlace2.5D Case 3 (Table 3, PDF p.6): 8 dies (4 CPU, 4 DRAM), x32 UCIe bumps, 8448 nets, 39 mm x 39 mm interposer, 0.6 whitespace. Thermal-aware optimization, Table 6 (PDF p.7).

thermal_observable.location: Maximum temperature (Tmax) of the HotSpot steady-state thermal map of the final ATPlace2.5D thermal-aware Case 3 placement (Table 6). The paper does not say which layer it is read from.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum over the thermal grid of the steady-state map under worst-case chiplet power. TAP-2.5D on the same case reports 94.1 degC.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper models a 3D-structured 2.5D package: passive interposer with TSVs, RDL and microbumps, epoxy fill, TIM, spreader and an air-forced heatsink. A simplified 2D steady-state Studio model cannot represent these through-thickness layers explicitly.
The paper's thermal solver is HotSpot 6.0 (64x64 grid) plus a fitted compact model. A different Studio solver and mesh will not reproduce the 92.3 degC value, so numerical comparison is invalid.

No final Case 3 placement is published in the pinned files: Case3.pl holds placeholder (0,0) coordinates for all 8 chiplets. The final layout appears only as Fig. 5 images, so the paper's Tmax cannot be tied to explicit coordinates.

The pinned thermal/hotspot.config does not match the paper text. It sets r_convec to 0.01 K/W versus the paper's 0.1 K/W, and spreader and heatsink sides of 0.03 m and 0.06 m versus the paper's 2x interposer-edge scaling (a 39 mm interposer exceeds a 30 mm spreader). It also sets model_type to block while the paper uses a 64x64 grid, and the secondary path is off. Ambient 318.15 K (45 degC) and the 64x64 grid_rows/grid_cols entries do match the paper.

The optimizer (analytical CGD with MILP and Bayesian hyperparameter tuning) and the thermal-penalty objective, which trades off wirelength and Tmax, cannot be replicated by a Studio thermal run. Studio would evaluate a fixed placement only.

The paper treats steady-state worst-case power only, with no transient behavior, no controller, no DTM and no reliability analysis, and it ignores temperature dependence of the parameters. Dynamic or time-varying use of the setup would be outside the published scope.

The paper imposes adiabatic lateral surfaces and the primary heat path only, ignoring the secondary substrate/PCB path. The compact model additionally assumes infinite space and quasi-homogeneous materials, which causes errors at chiplet edges and the interposer boundary (MAE about 1.25 degC for Case 3).
Final chiplet coordinates are not supplied by the reference files; generated shelf positions illustrate a 2D power snapshot, not the published placement.

studio_assumptions: Any Studio run for Case 3 uses a separate illustrative 2D placement and a one-row power trace built from the pinned dimensions and powers (CPU 8 mm x 9 mm at 150 W each, DRAM 9 mm x 9 mm at 20 W each). Its coordinates are generated by the runner and are not paper-derived.
Generated Studio temperatures are not compared numerically with the paper's 92.3 degC, and exact replication is not claimed.
Case3.pl has overlapping or out-of-bounds input positions; a deterministic nonoverlapping shelf layout was generated.
The public package says final placement is produced by its encrypted kernel, not by the supplied .pl input.
The power trace is one constant row made from source per-chiplet watts.

methods.note: Paper methods (pp.2-6) are verified: HotSpot 6.0 steady state, 64x64 grid, analytical Green's-function compact model (Eq. 12), MILP init, CGD, MILP legalization. But the experiment is a custom_2d_steady shelf layout, which does not match the paper's 3D-layered 2.5D stack (interposer/TSV/RDL/microbump/TIM/spreader/heatsink) or its placement optimizer. Calling it a reproduction of the 92.3 C Case 3 result is contradicted.

code.note: The pinned repo contains reproduce.py, but its compact model and placeflow_core are in files outside the supplied excerpts, and the repo states the final placement comes from an encrypted kernel. No paper-linked code availability statement exists in the PDF, and a bare repo URL is not evidence. Nothing shows that the code reproduces Table 6 Case 3.

parameters.note: Paper: r_convec 0.1 K/W, spreader/heatsink 2x interposer edge. Pinned hotspot.config: r_convec 0.01, s_spreader 0.03 m, s_sink 0.06 m, model_type block, model_secondary 0. These conflict and the authoritative value is unresolved. Layer properties are only inherited from refs [6,36], which are not supplied. Ambient 45 C and 64x64 grid do match the paper.

config.note: hotspot.config disagrees with the paper (0.01 vs 0.1 K/W, 30 mm spreader smaller than the 39 mm interposer, block vs 64x64 grid). The Studio floorplan (a 4x2 shelf, 32 mm x 18 mm bounding box on a 39 mm interposer) is a generated illustrative layout, not the published Fig. 5 placement. Case3.pl is all (0,0) placeholders. No Studio material/package spec is supplied.

data.note: Block dimensions (8x9 mm CPU, 9x9 mm DRAM) and per-block powers (150 W x4, 20 W x4) cover all 8 blocks in the same Case3 scenario, and the p.8 Fig. 5 caption partly cross-checks them. But units (um, W) are inferred rather than stated in the files. The final placement coordinates, nets file, bump offsets, layer-wise properties, and per-chiplet temperatures are unavailable. Fig. 5 is image-only, was not visually verified, and cannot be digitized. Tmax 92.3 C (Table 6) is verified as text, but the layer is unspecified. Powers are constant, steady, and not a published trace.

findings.reason: Shelf coordinates are generated, not paper-derived. Case3.pl is placeholder (0,0) and Fig. 5 is not digitized, so the 92.3 C result cannot be tied to this geometry.
The paper says 0.1 K/W but the pinned config sets r_convec 0.01 K/W, a 10x contradiction with an unresolved authority.
The paper states 2x scaling relative to the interposer (39 mm), but the config uses 30 mm spreader and 60 mm sink, so the spreader is smaller than the interposer.
The paper uses a 64x64 grid HotSpot, but the config has model_type block and model_secondary 0. Whether the published numbers used this config is unproven.
The um unit for blocks and W for power are inferred (not stated in files). The conversion factor 8000.000000000001 appears in a duplicate entry (a float artifact).
A 2D steady model cannot represent the paper's through-thickness TSV/RDL/microbump/epoxy/TIM/heatsink stack, which is a decisive feature of the reported Tmax.
The paper's placement result comes from CGD with a fitted compact model and MILP/Optuna. A fixed-layout 2D thermal evaluation is not a reproduction of the placement or Pareto behavior.
The PDF has no code/data availability statement, the repo notes an encrypted kernel, and a pinned repo URL alone does not establish that the final inputs exist.
Only pdftotext output was provided. Figures (Figs. 4-8) and table layouts were not visually verified, and Fig. 5 is the only source of the Case 3 layout.

The column is headed '%' but Case 3 reads 0.6, a unit ambiguity. Case 2 interposer is 55x52 mm in the paper vs 32x32 mm in reproduce.py, and Case 4 is 57x59 vs 37x37, indicating script/paper mismatches.

assessment.summary: Scenario: ATPlace2.5D Case 3 (4 CPU and 4 DRAM chiplets, 39 mm interposer, thermal-aware optimization). The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only. The input gate passed and simulation_allowed is true, while the scientific gate failed and the result was not independently verified. Studio ran: the custom 2D steady run completed (run 29195ae9542e4a0cac68f18d2d8d46e3) with a completed +1 W sensitivity run on CPU2_0. As a custom steady run, it has no transient trace. The input comes from pinned PKU-IDEA/ATPlace_pub commit 782b89ba6fe494bd50f075dff8019971133ec7c5, Case3. It uses Case3.blocks sizes (CPU 8x9 mm at 150 W, DRAM 9x9 mm at 20 W, with units inferred as um and W) and a generated placement. The placement assumption is a deterministic non-overlapping shelf layout (CPUs in one row, DRAMs in the row above), because Case3.pl holds only (0,0) placeholders and the final placement exists only as Fig. 5 images. The input.flp and the one-row constant input.ptrace are therefore illustrative, not paper-derived. Studio used bundled example.materials and package.config. In the Studio steady result, the hottest block was CPU2_2 at 96.36 C (369.51 K), with CPU2_3 at 96.09 C, CPU2_1 at 94.78 C and CPU2_0 at 88.24 C. DRAM blocks ranged from 59.68 to 65.29 C. Adding 1 W to CPU2_0 raised it from 361.39 K to 361.6 K, about +0.21 K, so the response is directionally sensible. The paper's Tmax of 92.3 C (TAP-2.5D 94.1 C) is a HotSpot 6.0 64x64 steady-state maximum over an unspecified layer for the final optimized placement. It is not compared numerically with the Studio values, because comparison_valid is false: the placement, solver and mesh, package stack and heatsink boundary, and the observable location and aggregation do not match. Qualitatively, the Studio run shows the CPUs dominating the thermal map and a strong dependence on neighbor spacing and layout, which is consistent with the motivation for thermal-aware placement. The run is exploratory only and does not replicate or validate the paper; exact replication is not claimed.
limitations: Gate outcome: illustrative_2d_only. comparison_valid is false, the scientific gate failed, and the result is not independently verified; many evidence items lack page or asset locators and the adversarial reviews are unresolved.

The chiplet placement is generated (shelf layout), not the paper's optimized placement. Case3.pl is placeholder-only and Fig. 5 is image-only, so Studio temperatures cannot represent the paper's layout.

Studio's 2D model with bundled materials and package config cannot reproduce the paper's 3D package stack (interposer with TSVs, RDL and microbumps, epoxy, TIM, spreader, air-forced heatsink), so layer-wise heat paths differ.
Solver and mesh mismatch: the paper uses HotSpot 6.0 with a 64x64 grid plus a fitted Green's-function compact model, whereas Studio uses a different solver and mesh.

Observable mismatch: the paper's 92.3 C is a maximum over the thermal grid at an unstated layer, while Studio reports per-block temperatures (die, interface, spreader and heatsink nodes). Location and aggregation are not matched.

Boundary conditions disagree: the paper states heatsink convective resistance of 0.1 K/W with adiabatic lateral surfaces, whereas pinned hotspot.config sets 0.01 K/W, a 30 mm spreader and a 60 mm sink, block model type and no secondary path. The authoritative values are unclear.
Block dimension and power units in the pinned files are inferred (um and W), and the power is a single constant snapshot; no power time series is published.
Only a single paper Tmax is reported, with no per-chiplet temperatures, so there is no per-block reference to compare with.
The optimizer (MILP, conjugate-gradient analytical placement, Bayesian tuning) and its wirelength versus Tmax tradeoff are not exercised by Studio, which evaluates a fixed layout.
The run is steady-state only: no transient behavior, controller, DTM, or temperature-dependent parameters, so nothing about dynamic behavior can be concluded.
The sensitivity check (+1 W on CPU2_0 gives about +0.21 K) tests only local self-heating response in the illustrative layout and does not validate absolute temperatures.

The paper models a 3D-structured 2.5D package: passive interposer with TSVs, RDL and microbumps, epoxy fill, TIM, spreader and an air-forced heatsink. A simplified 2D steady-state Studio model cannot represent these through-thickness layers explicitly.
The paper's thermal solver is HotSpot 6.0 (64x64 grid) plus a fitted compact model. A different Studio solver and mesh will not reproduce the 92.3 degC value, so numerical comparison is invalid.

No final Case 3 placement is published in the pinned files: Case3.pl holds placeholder (0,0) coordinates for all 8 chiplets. The final layout appears only as Fig. 5 images, so the paper's Tmax cannot be tied to explicit coordinates.

The pinned thermal/hotspot.config does not match the paper text. It sets r_convec to 0.01 K/W versus the paper's 0.1 K/W, and spreader and heatsink sides of 0.03 m and 0.06 m versus the paper's 2x interposer-edge scaling (a 39 mm interposer exceeds a 30 mm spreader). It also sets model_type to block while the paper uses a 64x64 grid, and the secondary path is off. Ambient 318.15 K (45 degC) and the 64x64 grid_rows/grid_cols entries do match the paper.

The optimizer (analytical CGD with MILP and Bayesian hyperparameter tuning) and the thermal-penalty objective, which trades off wirelength and Tmax, cannot be replicated by a Studio thermal run. Studio would evaluate a fixed placement only.

The paper treats steady-state worst-case power only, with no transient behavior, no controller, no DTM and no reliability analysis, and it ignores temperature dependence of the parameters. Dynamic or time-varying use of the setup would be outside the published scope.

The paper imposes adiabatic lateral surfaces and the primary heat path only, ignoring the secondary substrate/PCB path. The compact model additionally assumes infinite space and quasi-homogeneous materials, which causes errors at chiplet edges and the interposer boundary (MAE about 1.25 degC for Case 3).
Final chiplet coordinates are not supplied by the reference files; generated shelf positions illustrate a 2D power snapshot, not the published placement.

Any Studio run for Case 3 uses a separate illustrative 2D placement and a one-row power trace built from the pinned dimensions and powers (CPU 8 mm x 9 mm at 150 W each, DRAM 9 mm x 9 mm at 20 W each). Its coordinates are generated by the runner and are not paper-derived.
Generated Studio temperatures are not compared numerically with the paper's 92.3 degC, and exact replication is not claimed.
